paragraphs.text: On 11 November, S-1 Visa would cover school, undergraduate, and postgraduate education, while S-2 Visa would be for specified educational activities including PhD and research scholars in Bharatiya universities, visiting faculty, foreign research students coming to Bharat for research, scientific and anthropological expeditions, internships, and exchange students.
The production investment business visa for technical personnel was earlier granted under e-B4 visa nomenclature.
The Ministry of Home Affairs changed the name of tourist visas, and changed the name of tourist visas to visitor visas.
Major changes have been made in tourist and student visas among several other matters.
The tourist visa has been renamed to jitter visa.
The most discussed change happened in the tourist category yesterday.
There are clear provisions for school education, higher education, PhD, research, internships, and exchange programs.
Separate clear paths were created for treatment and studies yesterday.

Foreign nationals planning to come to Bharat were advised to definitely confirm the latest information related to their category, validity, and necessary documents from Griha or the official Bharatiya Visa portal before applying, so that there is no trouble at the time of travel yesterday.

"Significant changes to ease the visa system are continuously taking place under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and guidance of Union Home Minister Amit Shah," Ministry of Home Affairs said.
M-1 Visa would include other medical treatments besides Ayush systems, while M-3 Visa would be for treatment under Ayush systems yesterday.
There is a separate arrangement for the companion accompanying the patient — the companion of M-1 holder would get M-2 and the companion of M-3 holder would get M-4 Visa yesterday.
This is the second major change in the Visa system within two years yesterday.
The government studied visa systems of developed countries and global standards when considering the simplification of the Indian visa system, Ministry of Home Affairs said.
Ministry of Home Affairs stated that "The step aims at making it (visa regime) more compact, coherent and responsive to the requirements of foreign nationals visiting India".

The consolidation of similar purposes of travel is aimed at providing greater clarity and ease in identifying the appropriate visa category while facilitating legitimate foreign arrivals, Ministry spokesperson said.
Electronic visas or e-visas are processed by electronic travel authorization under 13 sub-categories.

Eligible foreign students taking admission in Indian institutions through the Study in India portal will be able to get a multiple entry e-visa for up to five years or the duration of the course, whichever is less, and both categories provide for a default one-year multiple entry visa. It will be for short-term activities, including business meetings, medical consultation, wellness retreats, short-term medical treatment, and short-term courses related to Bharatiya languages, music, art, and craft, and this includes all activities of V-1 along with mountaineering, for which a 6-month Visa will be given with multiple entry facility.
Both these Visas, including their E-Visa versions, would be issued as a default option for one year with multiple entry facility.
Separate visa categories have been fixed for attendants accompanying patients.

According to Mantri, this arrangement would provide convenience to those patients whose treatment involves multiple consultations, follow-up visits, or phased procedures, and it would also promote medical value tourism in Bharat.

Medical treatment categories include M-1 (other medical treatments, 1 year default, multiple entry), M-3 (Ayush treatments, 1 year default, multiple entry), along with companion Visas M-2 for M-1 holders and M-4 for M-3 holders.
The visa application forms had their columns reduced as part of the simplification.
The former tourist Visa has been renamed because the new name reflects not only traditional tourism but also a broader range of multiple approved purposes.
The Ministry of Home Affairs will update its IT systems by year-end to grant visas per new rationalisation.

Currently, the E-Visa facility is available to citizens of 172 countries, and 172 countries have access to e-visa facilities with an application process involving 13 sub-categories, Ministry of Home Affairs said. E-visa facility is currently available for citizens of 172 countries according to the ministry.
